Atlas Metrics — ESG data infrastructure for private markets.

Web App SaaS · B2B ESG Sustainability Risk management

Atlas Metrics is an ESG data infrastructure platform helping banks, funds, and businesses collect, analyze, and report non-financial data across complex regulatory frameworks like CSRD, SFDR, and the GHG Protocol.

The platform serves organizations navigating a landscape where compliance requirements evolve faster than most teams can keep up.

We turned a technically and regulatorily complex domain into something approachable, structured, and trustworthy, from the first data input to the final audit-ready report.

Problem space

ESG reporting sits at the intersection of regulatory pressure, data fragmentation, and organizational complexity. Most companies deal with:

  • dozens of overlapping frameworks with conflicting requirements
  • data scattered across subsidiaries, suppliers, and spreadsheets
  • sustainability teams under pressure to produce audit-ready reports with no reliable tooling

Most existing solutions were built for compliance departments, not for the people actually doing the work. The result: tools that were rigid, slow, and disconnected from real workflows.

Design approach

We shaped a platform that turns regulatory complexity into a clear, guided workflow, one that could serve a sustainability manager at a mid-size company and a risk analyst at a major bank within the same system. As the founding designer, the role extended beyond craft: contributing to roadmap decisions, shaping product priorities, and establishing the design processes that would support a growing team.

Design system

Built from 187 components, with variants, dropdown states and toggles for flexible builds. Tokens for color, text style, radius and spacing.

Product chapters

Rather than a single feature, Atlas was built as a connected suite. Each chapter solves a distinct problem in the ESG data journey.

  • Data Collection & Network. Connecting organizations and their value chains so data flows in without duplication or manual chasing. Suppliers, subsidiaries, and third parties can submit directly into the platform, with validation built into the collection layer.
  • Logic Builder & Custom Metrics. Letting teams define their own aggregation rules, critical for organizations with non-standard reporting structures. Formulas, weightings, and custom KPIs persist across reporting cycles without rebuilding from scratch.
  • Multi-standard Reporting. One dataset, any framework. Designed to eliminate the recurring rebuild that compliance reporting usually requires. CSRD, GRI, SFDR, and custom templates all draw from the same source, reducing both effort and inconsistency risk.
  • Carbon Accounting. Operational and financed emissions tracking aligned to PCAF and GHG Protocol. Scope 1, 2, and 3 calculations with methodology transparency and audit-ready output that holds up under external review.
  • Risk Engine. Real-time risk signal monitoring translated into portfolio-level visibility and early warnings. Configurable thresholds let teams surface what matters to them, whether regulatory, reputational, or operational, before it becomes a reporting problem.
  • Performance Monitoring & Dashboards. Customizable analytics for benchmarking and strategic decisions across portfolios and sectors. Designed for both the sustainability manager tracking progress and the executive who needs a clear signal at a glance.
  • Materiality Analysis. Automated double materiality assessments with survey flows, scoring, and clear prioritization views. Turns what is typically a months-long consulting engagement into a repeatable internal process.

Case study: Scaling past the consulting team

Atlas grew from an early-stage product into a platform serving hundreds of organisations across banks, funds and portfolio companies. The gap between what the product did and what customers needed was absorbed by people: an in-house ESG consulting team who ran workshops, set up accounts, answered questions and did by hand whatever the app didn't do yet. It worked, but it didn't scale. Every new customer meant more consultant hours, and the team couldn't keep growing in step.

Impact

Building Atlas from zero to acquisition meant designing through every stage of a product's life, from rough early concepts with no users to a mature platform trusted by financial institutions across 15+ countries.

The challenge was never any single feature. It was maintaining coherence, quality, and user trust across a product that kept expanding in every direction.
